newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover fell in week to July 11.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover fell in week to July 11.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Monday its turnover dropped 28.31 percent in the week ending July with its short-term debentures index standing at 192.02.
Total turnover in 103 transactions fell to 108.038 million dinars ($18.65 million) from 150.712 million dinars in 135 deals a week ago when the BSE debentures index stood at 183.11.
The BSE short-term debentures index mirrors conditions under which companies and banks borrow and repay their debt.
It is calculated on volume, interest rate and maturity of the most bourse-traded short-term commercial papers and treasury bills. Index base is 1996.
For the week ending July 11, the BSE reported following details:
* Commercial paper accounted for 92 transactions worth 13.238 million dinars.
* Treasury bills in one deal traded for 0.25 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between 6.0 and 12 percent per month, while maturity stood between seven and 30 days.
* There were five transactions in the central bank short-term bonds worth 60 million dinars.
* In three transactions, Yugoslav government sold 34.154 million dinars worth of its first 50-million dinars tranche T-bills with 30-day maturity and a 3.5 percent monthly interest rate.
The Yugoslav government launched a second 200 million dinars issue of 30-, 60- and 90-day T-bills on July 10 to finance federal budget.
* Two deals were in certificates of deposit in the volume of 0.4 million dinars.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper and treasury bills rose to 59.277 million dinars from 40.587 million the previous week.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, increased to 32.950 million dinars from 17.45 million. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 311 4254
